title: to, do
parentNote: Two more words we learn whole today, and they are a pair: to and do rhyme with each other, and the o in both of them says oo. That is a job the o does in barely a dozen words in English and this course never teaches it as a rule, so these two are simply remembered. The slip to expect is a careful child reading them as toe and doe, which is exactly what everything they have learned so far predicts — don't correct the thinking, just say "these two say oo" and carry on. They are worth a whole day because of the grammar they open up. to lets your child finally write where somebody is going and why they are doing a thing — ran to the barn, want to help — and do turns a sentence into a question: Do they want a cake? Until today there was no way to ask one.

activities.sentence: I did run to the shed to get a spade.
activities.prompt: Do not sound this one out. The o says oo: to.
No sounding out. Look at it and say it: to.

activities.sentence: Do they want to see the hamster?
activities.prompt: The same trick with a d on the front. Not doe — do.
Look at it and say it: do. Then say to. They rhyme.
Three jobs an o can do. In to and do it does none of them, which is why we just learn them.
This is the sound to and do actually say — the oo in flute and tune. They just spell it with an o.
No new sound today, so these are all words you can already sound out.
The longest one. Two a words stuck together, and only the second one has a quiet e after it.
Both say oo. Only the first letter tells them apart, so listen hard at the front.
These three get muddled up a lot. Listen to the front, then the middle.

activities.text: I want to run up the path to the barn.
Do they want to see the hamster in the shed?
Fern did run to the garden to get a spade and a fork.
I do not want to stop, and I do not want to rest!

activities.title: The cake I want to make
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: I want to make a cake for Mum.
Dad did help. I did crack three eggs in a red pot.
Then I did stir it, and stir it, and stir it.
Dad did set the pot in the stove.
I want to see it. I do not want to sit still.
I did peek in the stove, and then I did peek in it a lot.
The cake did not lift up. The cake is flat.
Dad did grin. A flat cake is still a cake.
I did add red jam on the top, and then Mum came in.
Mum did munch it up. Do I want to make a cake for Dad? I do!

questions.prompt: I want to make a cake for ...

At the end I want to make a cake for ...
